qt: to the Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy Kostas Papadakis (NI), Lefteris Nikolaou-Alavanos (NI) Subject:

As the genocide of the Palestinian people by the occupier, Israel, continues with relentless intensity, the US and Britain have started launching air strikes in Yemen. These attacks are simply pouring fuel on the fire, exacerbating the ongoing imperialistic war in Yemen, heightening tensions in the Red Sea and stoking the ever-fiercer competition for control over a wider area of strategic importance. In view of this, can the Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative answer the following: 1.

What is his position regarding the fact that, despite the proclamations about ‘peace and stability’, the genocide of the Palestinian people by Israel, along with EU-NATO interference in Yemen and the Red Sea with the EU's all-out backing, constitute a dangerous escalation in the ongoing conflicts in the Middle East, with the blood of the people being shed to promote Euro-Atlantic imperialistic interests?

What is his position regarding the fact that Euro-Atlantic powers are using shipping as a pretext for pushing their plans and for control of the area, in a context where they are facing tough confrontation from rivals?

What is his position regarding the fact that Israel's occupation of the Palestinian territories and the slaughter going on in the Gaza Strip and Saudi-Arabia's ongoing US-backed war in Yemen, are critical problems that are leading to the explosive situation in the Red Sea, increasing the risk of a wider flare-up, putting the lives of ship workers at risk and sending energy prices through the roof, while shipowners make a tidy profit from lucrative charterparties?

(15 May 2024) The EU is gravely concerned by the humanitarian crisis in Gaza. The EU reiterates the importance of ensuring the protection of all civilians at all times in line with international humanitarian law, the release of all hostages, and the delivery of aid to those in need. The EU provides urgent humanitarian aid in Gaza and is also fully mobilised to prevent further escalation in the region and to revive the political process towards a lasting and sustainable peace based on the two-state solution. The EU supports Yemen’s territorial integrity and unity and its internationally recognised Government and underlines the importance of the Presidential Leadership Council unity. The EU is one of Yemen’s biggest donors of humanitarian aid (more than EUR 1.3 billion for 2015-2023). At the same time, the EU has continuously condemned the Houthi attacks against commercial ships as unacceptable violations of international law threatening maritime security, peace and stability in the region, and underlined that they must stop, notably through the High Representative’s declaration on behalf of the EU and its Member States of 12 January 2024 (1), welcoming the 10 January 2024 United Nations Security Council resolution 2722 (2) condemning the Houthi attacks. Operation ‘Prosperity Guardian’ is a United States-led multinational military operation to respond to Houthi-led attacks on shipping in the Red Sea. Neither the EU nor the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation are part of this operation. On 8 February 2024, the Council adopted Decision 2024/583 (3) to establish a new defensive EU maritime operation (Aspides), which contributes to the freedom of navigation in the Red Sea and beyond. This operation aims at protecting merchant vessels, without any engagement on Yemen’s soil.
